messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview: permissions audit log improvements
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview is enhancing audit logging for role-based access control, adding two new audit operations to improve transparency and troubleshooting. The update, rolling out worldwide from late September to mid-November 2026, requires no action but helps administrators better investigate access issues and monitor compliance.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

To improve transparency and troubleshooting for Microsoft Purview role-based access control (RBAC), we are enhancing audit logging for permission checks performed in the Microsoft Purview portal. These new audit records will provide administrators with clearer visibility into role and scoped-role authorization decisions, helping them investigate access issues and better understand how access evaluations are performed.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 569363.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late September 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Purview administrators and compliance administrators who review audit logs for access investigations and troubleshooting

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview portal
  • Microsoft Purview Audit

What will happen

  • New audit records will be generated when access checks are performed in the Microsoft Purview portal.
  • Two new audit operations will be available:
    • CheckUsersInRoles
    • CheckUserInRolesWithScopes
  • Administrators will be able to review these audit records as part of SecurityComplianceRBAC audit activities.
  • The enhancement is enabled by default and requires no configuration.
  • Audit records will only be generated for access checks that occur after the feature is deployed.
  • No historical or retroactive audit records will be created for prior access checks.
  • There is no impact for organizations.
  • Supported permission-assignment and role-group change audit records will include the ClientPortal field within PreExecutionMessage, helping administrators distinguish changes initiated from Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender. 
    • Supported activities for portal attribution 
      • Permission assignments: Granting, updating, or removing permission assignments. 
      • Role groups: Creating, updating, or deleting role groups. 
  • Expected ClientPortal values: 
    • Microsoft Purview portal: "ClientPortal": "Microsoft Purview" 
    • Microsoft Defender portal: "ClientPortal": "Microsoft Defender" 

RBAC audit-CheckUserInRolesWithScopes:

RBAC audit-checkusersinroles:

Action required and recommendations

No action is required. We recommend that administrators:

  • Review internal monitoring and audit procedures to determine whether the new audit activities should be included in access investigations.
  • Inform compliance and security teams about the availability of the new audit operations.
  • Update any internal documentation or reporting processes that reference Microsoft Purview RBAC audit data.

Learn more

  • Permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable audit logging capabilities?Yes. The change enhances audit logging capabilities by adding two new audit operations.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Administrators gain additional audit visibility into RBAC access evaluation outcomes, improving monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview: Retirement of select DSPM partner integrations
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview will retire select DSPM partner integrations (Varonis, BigID, Cyera, OneTrust) for non-Microsoft data sources on December 7, 2026. These integrations will no longer ingest or display data, but other DSPM capabilities remain unaffected. No action is required, but review dependencies if using these integrations.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Effective December 7, 2026, we will retire the public preview experience for select non-Microsoft data sources in Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) through partner integrations.

The affected partner integrations are Varonis for Salesforce data, BigID for Databricks, Cyera for Snowflake, and OneTrust for Google Cloud Platform (GCP). We are evolving Microsoft Purview and rethinking how we bring non-Microsoft signals into the Purview experience.

This change applies only to the partner integrations listed above. Other Microsoft Purview DSPM capabilities are not affected.

Rollout schedule

The affected partner integrations will no longer be available beginning December 7, 2026.

This change applies to:

  • Worldwide
  • GCC
  • GCC High
  • DoD

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations participating in the public preview for connecting supported non-Microsoft data sources to Microsoft Purview DSPM through the affected partner integrations

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)

What will happen

Beginning December 7, 2026:

  • Organizations will no longer be able to connect the supported non-Microsoft data sources to Microsoft Purview DSPM through the affected partner integrations.
  • Data from those sources will no longer be ingested, processed, or displayed in Microsoft Purview DSPM through these integrations.
  • Other Microsoft Purview DSPM capabilities are not affected.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required.

If your organization currently uses these integrations, we recommend reviewing related internal processes or dependencies and updating them as needed before December 7, 2026.

Learn more

  • Learn about Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. After retirement, data from the affected non-Microsoft sources will no longer be ingested, processed, or displayed in DSPM through these integrations.
